summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored documents from small jurisdictions (Netherlands, Qatar, Botswana, Indonesia, Korea, Turks and Caicos, Taiwan). Mostly laws, regulations and official pages: they add rules (program_terms) and dated events rather than statistics; the only new numbers are four Indonesian golden-visa figures (corporate-investor amount and share, other categories, 61 nationalities). Points for review: (1) event e-fe5e582a07 (Botswana, 17 Dec 2025) says Parliament 'approves' the Citizenship Amendment Bill, but its source says the vote passed the SECOND READING and the bill went to committee stage; title/description should be corrected. (2) Turks and Caicos Home Owner's Permit (US$300,000 home, 5 years) is a separate permit with no programme row; its terms are filed under tca-investor-residence-permit with route names starting home_owner_permit, a separate programme row may be preferable. (3) qat-almeezan-law-10-2018: the stored HTML lacks the article texts; ledger partial. (4) Botswana has no programme row; no rows needed program_id for it in this pass.

events.title: Vreemdelingencirculaire B11/2.2 rewritten after the investor scheme ended
events.description: WBV 2024/10 (signed 24 Apr 2024, Staatscourant 26 Apr 2024, in force the day after publication) states that the policy ended on 17 April 2024: new applications are refused, applications filed before 17 April 2024 are still handled under the old rules, and renewals of existing permits remain possible. The explanatory note cites EU concerns about money laundering and the amendment of the Vreemdelingenbesluit (Staatsblad 2024, 83 of 16 April 2024).
events.quote: Verlengingsaan- vragen van bestaande verblijfsvergunningen als vermogende vreemdeling blijven ook na 17 april 2024 mogelijk.

events.title: 12th investment immigration councils discuss public-project thresholds
events.description: The 12th investment immigration working council and investment immigration council (Justice, Finance, Foreign Affairs, Interior, Industry, Land, Culture ministries, Financial Services Commission and two private members) met between 14 and 22 June 2023 and prepared the increase of the public-project thresholds.

events.title: Designated areas of the real-estate investment scheme extended by three years
events.description: The scheme in Jeju, Incheon (Songdo, Yeongjong, Cheongna), Busan (Haeundae, East Busan), Pyeongchang (Alpensia) and Yeosu (Gyeongdo) was due to lapse on 30 April 2023 (Busan on 19 May 2023); despite weak results in some areas, all were extended by three years from 1 May 2023 (notice to be amended in May 2023).
events.quote: 제주, 인천(송도‧영종‧청라), 부산(해운대‧동부산), 평창(알펜시아), 여수(경도) 지역의 시행기간을 3년 연장합니다.

events.title: Ministry announces plan to tighten permanent residence for investment immigrants
events.description: The Ministry said it would tighten the requirements for permanent residence obtained through investment immigration (e.g. a residence requirement), because investors withdrew their money right after getting permanent residence and permanent residence carries local voting rights.
events.quote: 투자이민으로 영주권을 취득한 후 투자금을 바로 회수하는 사례 등 그간 지적된 문제점들을 개선하기 위해 투자이민 영주자격의 요건을 강화할 예정입니다.

events.title: Immigration Review Commission reports abuses in Belongership and PRC grants
events.description: The Immigration Review Commission appointed in 2003 (chaired by Don-Hue Gardiner) reported in February 2004, identifying Belonger status given for political favours and PRC applications ignored or delayed for months or years, and recommended an independent Citizenship Commission and clear criteria; according to the 2009 Commission of Inquiry little or nothing came of it.
events.quote: including instances of Belonger status given blatantly in return for political favours

events.title: Cabinet grants Belonger status to a golf-course developer with a peppercorn Crown Land lease
events.description: The Commission of Inquiry reports that by 29 November 2006 Cabinet decided to grant 238.72 acres for a proposed golf course at a rent of $1 per acre per year and at the same time approved Belonger status for the developer, removing the need for a Belonger partner in the project.
events.quote: At the same time they approved the grant of Belonger status for Mr Hoffmann. The effect of this grant was to avoid the need for Mr Hoffmann to engage any other Belonger partner in the project

events.title: Commission of Inquiry recommends removing ministers from grants of Belongership and PRCs
events.description: Sir Robin Auld recommends removing ministerial involvement from the grant or revocation of immigration status (Belongership, Permanent Residence Certificates, residence and work permits), decisions under clear statutory criteria by an independent body or public servants, with a merits appeal; and endorses the 2004 proposal of an independent Citizenship Commission.
events.location: PDF p. 109 (printed p. 108), para 3.75; PDF p. 242, recommendation 62
events.quote: I consider that there is urgent need for removal of ministerial involvement in the exercise of discretionary or other powers concerning the grant or revocation of immigration status.

events.title: New Immigration Ordinance and Regulations in force with investor PRC and residence routes
events.description: Immigration Ordinance 19 of 2015 and the Immigration Regulations (L.N. 28/2016) came into force on 1 April 2016, setting PRC investor routes (home, business, designated public sector project, US$1 million home or business), the Governor's undertaking, a quota for investment PRCs to be gazetted, the investor Residence Permit (condition B) and a new Home Owner's Permit.
events.location: PDF p. 1, contents of the revised edition; PDF p. 75

events.title: Failing to retain the investment becomes a ground to revoke a PRC
events.description: Ordinance 14 of 2018, in force 3 August 2018, added to section 25 of the Immigration Ordinance a ground for revoking a Permanent Residence Certificate where the holder failed to retain the investment used in the application, as prescribed.
events.location: PDF p. 1 (contents) and PDF p. 25, s. 25(j)
events.quote: that P has failed to retain an investment used in an application for a Permanent Residence Certificate that has been issued, as prescribed; or (Inserted by Ord. 14 of 2018)

events.title: Regulations for Hong Kong and Macao residents first issued
events.description: The Ministry of the Interior issued the full text (38 articles) of the regulations on entry, residence and registered permanent residence of Hong Kong and Macao residents on 30 June 1997; amended many times since (full texts 1999, 2009, 2013, 2018). Whether the 1997 text already had an investment ground is not stated.
events.quote: On June 30, 1997, the Ministry of the Interior (86) Order No. 8680202 issued a full text of 38 Articles

gaps: qat-almeezan-law-10-2018: article texts of Law 10/2018 not in the stored copy
TCA: no programme row for the Home Owner's Permit (Immigration Regulations regs 33-37)
TCA: investment-PRC quota under reg 23 is to be published in the Gazette; no gazetted quota among stored documents

ledger.contains: Staatscourant 2024 nr. 13488 (26 Apr 2024): decision WBV 2024/10 rewriting Vreemdelingencirculaire B11/2.2 on the wealthy-foreigner (foreign investor) permit: policy ended 17 Apr 2024, pending applications and renewals still handled; conditions (EUR 1,250,000 in an innovative company, partnership or SEED fund; Dutch/EU bank; RVO added-value test with primary and secondary criteria incl. 10 fte in 5 years; FIU check; no residential property); explanatory note on the reasons (money laundering risk) and Staatsblad 2024, 83. No statistics.

Al Meezan web page for Law No. 10 of 2018 on Permanent Residence: law card (type law, no. 10, date printed 04/09/2018, 13 articles, in force, Official Gazette issue 15 of 21/10/2018, p. 3), the preamble (laws consulted) and a list of article links. The texts of the 13 articles are not in the stored copy (the page loads them separately). No numbers extracted: the card data repeat what other sources already give (publication 21 Oct 2018).
ledger.to_do: Stored HTML holds only the law card and preamble; the article texts (incl. art. 4 annual cap and eligibility conditions) are missing. Obtain a copy with the article texts (e.g. the PDF or Word download on Al Meezan) and extract the rules. Note: the Hijri date printed beside 04/09/2018 (13/12/1438) does not match that Gregorian year; no issue-date event added.

ledger.contains: Aqarat (Real Estate Regulatory Authority) web page on property ownership by non-Qataris: two classes of real-estate residence (first class: property of at least QAR 3,650,000 / US$1,000,000 with permanent-residency benefits for health, education and investment; second class: QAR 730,000 / US$200,000, residence tied to the property), one-stop window, general claims about the real estate sector (first globally in ease of registration, documents in less than a day). Both thresholds are already in program_terms from this source; nothing else in scope.

Qatar Tourism instruction manual on Cabinet Decision 28 of 2020 (non-Qatari ownership and use of real estate under Law 16 of 2018): freehold vs usufruct (up to 99 years, extendable), 25 areas (9 freehold, 16 usufruct; also called twenty-six in the text) with zone tables and maps, ownership outside the areas (shops in commercial complexes, one unit per residential complex), inheritance (one housing property up to 3,000 m2), residency conditions (above QAR 730,000 real-estate residency; above QAR 3,650,000 with permanent-residency benefits; below 730,000 no residency), how to apply (Ministry of Justice e-service, offices at The Pearl and Lusail), FAQ (aggregation of several properties, build on vacant land within 4 years, registration fee 0.25%). Zone numbers and area counts are not programme statistics and are not recorded as numbers.

US State Department 2025 Investment Climate Statement for Qatar (28 pp.): general investment climate, FDI law, sectors, taxation, dispute settlement, SOEs and QIA, labour, etc. In scope only the paragraphs on property-linked residency (p. 4: residency while owning property, 90 days a year, QAR 730,000 / US$1 million values; p. 15: residency by property value and location, Cabinet Resolution 28/2020, Office for Non-Qatari Real Estate Ownership). Naturalisation after 25 years capped at 50 a year and the Jusour Mustaqel independent visa (March 2024, p. 27-28) are not investment programmes and are not extracted; the rest is out of scope (macro and FDI figures).

BOPA/Daily News report (16 Dec 2025) of the Minister of Labour and Home Affairs presenting the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2025: multiple citizenship and citizenship by investment; investors could apply immediately (unlike dual citizenship, waiting period of up to 10 years, not a programme number); a set amount to be invested within an agreed period, amount not yet decided; vetting by security organs; loss of citizenship for breach; target sectors (manufacturing, mining and energy, agriculture, infrastructure, financial services, green economy); excluded rights (vote, public office, free state education, government funding, state or tribal land, disciplined forces); money to go to an Economic Citizenship fund; MPs' views. No programme amounts. Already covered by event e-7dd8f68854; nothing to add.

BOPA/Daily News report (18 Dec 2025): on 17 Dec 2025 the majority of MPs voted for the Citizenship Amendment Bill 2025, which then passed the SECOND READING and went to the committee stage (not final passage); multiple citizenship for high-end investors; section 4 target sectors (manufacturing, mining and energy, agriculture, infrastructure, financial services, tourism, technology and digitalisation, sport and creatives, health, green and renewable energy, others prescribed); economic citizens denied the vote; MPs' objections (no cap on other citizenships, corruption, passport value; permanent residence as alternative). No numbers. Already covered by event e-fe5e582a07, whose title/description (Parliament approves the bill) overstates the stage: see summary.

Botswana Government Extraordinary Gazette Supplement B, 12 Dec 2025, pp. B.843-B.844: National Registration (Amendment) Bill 2025 (Bill No. 35), consequential to the Citizenship (Amendment) Bill: replaces dual citizen with multiple citizen and defines economic citizenship (citizenship granted solely for economic investment); commencement by ministerial order. No numbers. Covered by event e-5485c60988.

Immigration press release (2 Feb 2026) comparing Global Citizen of Indonesia (GCI, issued January 2026: unlimited stay for ex-citizens, their descendants to the second degree and spouses/children of citizens, report every 5 years, a lighter investment guarantee in bonds, shares, funds, deposits or property, minimum income about USD 1,500 a month or USD 15,000 a year; skills route without investment) with Golden Visa Indonesia (since 2024; 5 or 10 years, renewable; individual investor, corporate investor, second home, global talent, world figures; investment amounts US$2.5m/5m with a company, US$25m/50m corporate, US$350,000/700,000 in bonds, listed shares or deposits). GCI is a diaspora scheme with no programme row and no stated investment amount, so its income figures are not recorded; the six golden visa amounts were already in program_terms; permit validity added.

Immigration press release (26 Sep 2025): 1,012 golden visas issued to 23 Sep 2025, investment of more than Rp48 trillion (nearly Rp46.5 trillion or about 96% from foreign companies setting up subsidiaries/branches; Rp249.3 billion individual investors; Rp1.45 trillion other golden visa subjects), non-tax revenue Rp12.96 billion, holders from 61 countries, validity 5 to 10 years and benefits. Total, permits, fee revenue and individual-investor amount were already recorded; the other parts, share and nationality count added.

Immigration press release (21 May 2026): Rp52.1 trillion investment through golden visas to 18 May 2026 since launch on 25 Jul 2024, from 1,274 golden visas; three largest categories by investment (E28D corporate Rp50,884,158,768,681; E28C individual without company Rp179,387,571,947; E28B individual with company Rp130,274,964,522); top three nationalities (USA 160, China 147, Taiwan 110); benefits (5-10 years, no local sponsor, family) and categories (corporate and individual investors, global talent, second home, silver hair, personage, repatriation of ex-citizens and descendants, IKN investors). All numbers already in the data; nothing to add.

Ministry of Justice press release (HWP, 29 Jun 2023): public-project investment immigration thresholds raised from 29 Jun 2023 (general KRW 0.5bn to 1.5bn; high-value KRW 1.5bn to 3bn), retirement scheme (55+, KRW 0.3bn) abolished; table of the three schemes with start dates (May 2013, Oct 2014); 12th investment immigration councils 14-22 June 2023 and their membership; rationale (funds lent to SMEs at low interest; no change in 10 years; PR obtainable by deposit only); foreign comparison amounts converted to won from a 2022 MOJ study (Australia, New Zealand, Portugal, US: about other countries' programmes, not recorded). Thresholds and events were already in the data; holding period, minimum age and council event added.

Ministry of Justice web page on public-project investment immigration (captured 2026): what it is (F-2 then F-5 after 5 years), two types (principal-guaranteed interest-free fund run by the Korea Development Bank, principal only repaid after 5 years and lent to SMEs; profit-and-loss investment in designated tourism enterprise-city development projects), thresholds (KRW 1.5bn; KRW 3bn high-value), benefits for investor, spouse and unmarried children, effects (loans to SMEs and smart factories). No statistics.

Ministry of Justice press release (1 May 2023): real-estate investment immigration renamed tourism and resort facility investment immigration; threshold raised to KRW 1bn; designated areas (Jeju, Incheon, Busan, Pyeongchang, Yeosu) that were to lapse on 30 Apr / 19 May 2023 extended by 3 years; 11th investment immigration councils 19-28 Apr 2023; scheme since Feb 2010 (F-2, F-5 after 5 years); plan to tighten investor permanent residence. No statistics. Threshold, launch and change events were already recorded; holding period and two events added.

Report of the Turks and Caicos Islands Commission of Inquiry 2008-2009 (Sir Robin Auld, 31 May 2009, 266 pp.) into possible corruption by elected members: governance, Crown Land, public contracts, political donations, payments to named ministers, aircraft, casino, recommendations (interim direct rule, criminal sanctions, integrity, Crown Land, constitution). In scope only the immigration parts: statutory scheme of Belongership, Permanent Residence Certificates (incl. investment in a business or home) and permits (paras 3.64-3.66), complaints of PRCs and Belongership granted for bribes (3.67, already an event), 2004 Immigration Review Commission (3.70-3.74), recommendation to remove ministers from grants (3.75, 5.x, rec. 62), Belonger status granted to a golf-course developer (4.95), Immigration Department inefficiency and waived work permits for developers (4.235-4.237). The report gives no counts of PRCs or Belongerships granted and no programme money figures; the dollar figures in it concern Crown Land, loans and payments to ministers and are out of scope. Immigration fees as almost 10% of recurrent revenue 2005/06 (para 3.81) cover all work permits and immigration fees, not the investor routes, so not recorded.

Undated one-page flow chart (Ministry of Border Control and Employment / Invest Turks and Caicos) of the PRC application process for investment routes: application for undertaking and/or PRC to Invest TCI, certificate of undertaking, PRC application once the undertaking conditions are met, the investment completed and the contribution made; refusal with no appeal (decision final); fees ($1,500 admin fee, $25,000 PRC when applicable). No statistics.

Revised edition (law as at 31 Mar 2021, 232 pp.) of the TCI Immigration Ordinance Cap. 5.01 (Ord. 19 of 2015 as amended), designation of ports, Immigration Regulations (L.N. 28/2016 as amended to 2/2020) with Schedules 1-7 (forms, visa-exempt countries, fees incl. work-permit fee scales), Exemption Order and Detention Direction. In scope: PRC provisions (Ordinance ss. 20-28: lifetime validity, revocation grounds incl. 2-year absence and failure to retain the investment, child endorsement to 19, Governor's refusal final), regs 12-23 (PRC routes with investment amounts, 60% local employment for business route, refundable fee except USD 1,000, 5-year retention, 12-month reinvestment, notification and annual report with USD 1,500 fine, exemption before 15 Jun 2018, endorsements incl. 11-year spouse endorsement, undertakings, designated public projects, investment PRC quota to be gazetted), Residence Permit condition B (USD 500,000 / 250,000 by island, 1-10 years), Home Owner's Permit (USD 300,000 home, 5 years), Schedule 7 fees for PRCs and residence permits, Form 5 (undertaking application, image pages read by OCR: capital minimum USD 300,000, offshore equity) and Form 6 (certificate of undertaking). Out of scope: entry control, API, carriers, work permits and their fee scales, offences (fines are general), detention. Image-only form pages 122-127, 131, 133-143, 154-216 were OCRed; apart from Form 5 they are residence and work permit application forms with no programme amounts (the residence form asks for annual funding bands less than $75-150,000 / 150-250,000 / more than 250,000, an applicant questionnaire, not a rule). No statistics.

Official Chinese text (as amended 13 Jun 2022, 39 articles) of the Ministry of the Interior regulations on entry, residence and settlement of Hong Kong and Macao residents in Taiwan: entry permits and stays (ch. 2), residence grounds (art. 16, incl. item 5: investment of NT$6 million or more approved by the competent authority, or innovation/entrepreneurship), documents, guarantor (art. 18-19), refusal grounds and bar periods (art. 22), certificate validity and extension (art. 24-26), revocation (art. 28), settlement after a qualifying period (art. 29: 1 year continuous or 2 years with 270 days a year; 5 years with 183 days for the entrepreneur route), settlement documents and household registration. The NT$6 million threshold was already recorded; settlement period, validity and guarantor rules added. No statistics; the page lists no amendment details beyond the date.

NIA English translation (unofficial) of the Hong Kong and Macao residents regulations, full text of 6 Feb 2018 (18 pp.): amendment history 1997-2018, entry and stay, residence grounds incl. NT$6 million investment (art. 16(1)(5)), documents, guarantor, refusal, validity (investors 1-3 years), revocation, registered permanent residence after 1 year continuous or 2 years with 270 days a year, transitional rule for NT$5 million deposits before 10 June 2003. Amendment entries do not say what changed in the investment ground, so no events beyond the first issue. No statistics.

Official Chinese text of the Immigration Act (入出國及移民法) as amended 28 Jun 2023: entry and exit, unregistered nationals (art. 9(6): residence for investment of a certain amount), foreigners' stay, residence (art. 23(1)(5): investors or representatives of foreign corporate investors with an approved investment of a certain amount; residence certificate up to 3 years), permanent residence (art. 25: 5 years with 183 days a year; art. 25(4): investment immigration with PR once the investment is approved and made; family may accompany; investment residence exempt from quotas), revocation of PR for average stay under 183 days over five years (art. 33(4)), subsidiary rules on investment objects and fund management (art. 35), immigration agencies and investment-immigration funds (art. 56) with fines (art. 79), deportation, detention, marriage brokerage, penalties. The Act sets no investment amount. Investment-immigration rules with numbers recorded as terms; no statistics.
